input.name: Free workspace job leak
input.overview: Free users are correctly capped to 3 assigned roles per company on GET /api/board, but opening the company workspace (the positions panel behind the company-name link) lists every catalog job. Apply the same broadcast assignment filter there, and close the two leftover APIs that still dump the full catalog.
input.plan:
# Fix free-user company workspace listing all jobs

## What’s going wrong

Free plan contract from [docs/reference/entitlements-and-opportunities.md](docs/reference/entitlements-and-opportunities.md): **3 stable active roles per company**. `GET /api/board` already does this via [`apply_capacity_to_board_page`](relocation_jobs/broadcast/service.py) → [`apply_capacity_to_companies`](relocation_jobs/broadcast/apply.py). Tests assert `len(jobs) <= 3` in [`tests/web/test_personalized_board.py`](tests/web/test_personalized_board.py).

Clicking the Adyen name on the board opens `/company/<country>/adyen`. That page’s **Positions** list is loaded from `GET /api/mcp/companies/<country>/<company>/applications`, which walks **all** `matching_jobs` with no assignment filter:

```458:461:relocation_jobs/mcp/service.py
    positions: list[CompanyPositionApplication] = []
    for job in company_row.get("matching_jobs") or []:
        track = resolve_track(
```

That is the surface that shows “all the Opportunities” while the board card still shows 3.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  board["GET /api/board"] --> cap["broadcast apply_capacity"]
  cap --> three["3 assigned Adyen jobs"]
  click["Click company name"] --> ws["GET /api/mcp/.../applications"]
  ws --> allJobs["all matching_jobs"]
```

Two other login-gated reads have the same hole (not used by the current board UI, but any free session can call them):

- [`GET /api/jobs`](relocation_jobs/web/routes/jobs.py) — full flatten, no opportunity keys, no capacity
- [`GET /api/companies/<country>/<name>`](relocation_jobs/web/routes/companies.py) — raw catalog row including `matching_jobs`

## Intended visible set (free / non-admin)

Keep the board rule: only **broadcast-assigned** jobs, plus roles already assigned that later left the live catalog (`listing_unavailable`). Also keep roles the user already engaged (looking-to-apply from public `/jobs/<slug>/save`, applied, pinned) even if they are not in the current 3 — otherwise the LinkedIn save funnel in [job-syndication.md](docs/reference/job-syndication.md) would drop the saved role.

Do **not** list the rest of the company’s catalog. Mirror the board upgrade hint (`jobs_hidden_count`) on the workspace.

Full / grandfathered / admin: unchanged, all roles.

Do **not** 403 the workspace for companies outside `user_opportunities`. A public-job save can land on a company that is not one of the 10 sticky slots.

MCP `get_job_context(url)` stays callable for a specific URL (needed to reframe a saved/assigned role). The bug is **listing**, not single-job lookup.

## Implementation

**1. Shared visible-job filter in `broadcast/`** (owns capacity; MCP/web may import it)

Add a small helper, e.g. `visible_job_keys_for_company(user_id, country, company_name, jobs) -> (allowed_keys, hidden_count)`, wrapping existing `limits_for_user_id` + `_ensure_page_assignments` + `apply_capacity_to_companies` on a one-company list. Reuse; do not fork the assignment matching in MCP.

Engaged-but-unassigned keys: union assignment keys with tracking keys that are looking-to-apply / applied / pinned / rejected (rejected already has its own board bucket; workspace today skips not-for-me only — keep that).

**2. Filter in [`list_company_applications`](relocation_jobs/mcp/service.py)**

- After loading `matching_jobs`, keep only allowed keys.
- Add `jobs_hidden_count` (and maybe `upgrade_jobs`) on [`CompanyApplicationsResponse`](relocation_jobs/mcp/types.py).
- Admin/full: skip filter (`limits.unlimited`).

**3. Workspace UI** ([`relocation_jobs/static/js/company.js`](relocation_jobs/static/js/company.js) + [`company.html`](relocation_jobs/static/company.html))

If `jobs_hidden_count > 0`, show the same credit / Full Access hint the board card already has in [`CompanyCard.jsx`](frontend/src/CompanyCard.jsx) (lines 455–462). No need to invent a new paywall.

**4. Close leftover APIs**

- `GET /api/jobs`: resolve opportunity scope + `apply_capacity_to_board_page` the same way as `GET /api/board` (admin bypass unchanged). Existing admin tests that expect the full UK fixture keep working via `v2_auth_client`.
- `GET /api/companies/...`: do not return raw `matching_jobs` for capped users. Either omit that field or run it through the same helper. Admin/full keep full payload (catalog tests use admin).

**5. Tests**

- New free-user case in [`tests/web/test_mcp_company_workspace.py`](tests/web/test_mcp_company_workspace.py): company with >3 catalog jobs → applications API returns ≤3 assigned (+ engaged extras), `jobs_hidden_count > 0`.
- Full/admin still see every role.
- Public-save / looking-to-apply job that is not in the 3 assignments still appears.
- Free user `GET /api/jobs` does not return unassigned extra jobs.
- Existing board tests stay the source of truth for the 3-cap.

**6. Docs**

One sentence in [entitlements-and-opportunities.md](docs/reference/entitlements-and-opportunities.md) and [company-workspace.md](docs/reference/company-workspace.md): workspace position list uses the same assignment cap as the board.

Out of scope: remote board capacity (Adyen is relocation); deleting unused `fetchJobs()` in `api.js`; blocking MCP `get_job_context` by URL.

    country: str,
    company: str,
    *,
    user_id: int | None = None,
) -> CompanyApplicationsResponse:
    uid = user_id if user_id is not None else resolve_user_id()
    country_key = country.strip().lower()
    company_name = resolve_company_for_workspace(country_key, company)
    company_row = get_company(country_key, company_name)
    if company_row is None:
        raise LookupError(f"Company not found: {company}")

    tracking = load_job_tracking(uid, country=country_key)
    status_history = load_job_status_history(uid, country=country_key)
    app_rows = repo.list_applications_for_company(uid, country_key, company_name)
    profile = get_application_profile(user_id=uid)
    app_by_key = {
        (row.get("idempotency_key") or "").strip(): row
        for row in app_rows
        if (row.get("idempotency_key") or "").strip()
    }
    visible_jobs, jobs_hidden_count = visible_jobs_for_company(
        uid, country_key, company_name, list(company_row.get("matching_jobs") or []),
    )

    positions: list[CompanyPositionApplication] = []
    for job in visible_jobs:
        item = _company_position_from_job(

            country_key=country_key,
            company_name=company_name,

            tracking=tracking,
            status_history=status_history,
            app_by_key=app_by_key,
            profile=profile,
        )
        if item:
            positions.append(item)

    positions.sort(key=lambda item: (not item.pinned, not item.looking_to_apply, item.title.lower()))
    return CompanyApplicationsResponse(
        country=country_key,
        company=company_name,
        company_slug=repo.company_slug(company_name),
        positions=positions,
        jobs_hidden_count=jobs_hidden_count,

The board already capped a free user to **3 assigned Adyen roles**. Opening the company workspace listed every catalog job because that API never applied the same cap.

**What changed**

The workspace now uses the same broadcast assignments as the board. A free user sees:

- the 3 assigned roles
- plus any role they already engaged (looking-to-apply, applied, pinned, rejected) — so a public `/jobs/<slug>/save` does not disappear
- a “+N more roles waiting” credit / Full Access hint for the rest

Full Access, grandfathered, and admin still see every role.

The same filter is on the leftover dumps that were still returning the full catalog: `GET /api/jobs` and `GET /api/companies/<country>/<name>`.

Tests cover the workspace cap, keeping a looking-to-apply role outside the 3, Full Access seeing all jobs, and the two leftover APIs.
